title: Θηριακά, Ἀλεξιφάρμακα, Theriaca and Alexipharmaca; «Териака», «Противоядия»
author: Nicander of Colophon
genre: Didactic hexameter poems on venomous animals and poisons
edition: O. Schneider 1856, with scholia, public domain (https://archive.org/details/theriacaetalexi00schngoog); Gow–Scholfield 1953; Jacques, CUF 2002/2007.
ru_evidence: ru.wikipedia 'Никандр Колофонский': only Scythia/Caucasus excerpts, VDI 1947 no. 3, pp. 302–303. No full Russian translation found.
en_evidence: Gow & Scholfield 1953, CUP (review doi 10.1017/s0009840x00180710); Overduin 2015, Brill (Theriaca, doi 10.1163/9789004283602).
other_translations: French: Jacques, CUF (2002 Theriaca; Alexipharmaca vol. III).
value: The earliest surviving Greek works on venomous animals and poisons. A core source for ancient pharmacology, zoology and Hellenistic glossographic poetics, with rich scholia. Used by historians of medicine and Hellenistic poetry.
ai_feasibility: Medium. The vocabulary is notoriously obscure and full of glosses, and identifying plants and animals needs specialist checks. A good showcase for visible model disagreement.
